record.original_question: Does a group need to have a subnormal abelian series if every countable subgroup of it has such a series?

evidence.quote: Does a group need to have a subnormal abelian series if every countable subgroup of it has such a series?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A group $G$ is said to have a subnormal abelian series if there exists a finite chain of subgroups
$$\{1\} = G_0 \trianglelefteq G_1 \trianglelefteq \cdots \trianglelefteq G_n = G,$$
in which each $G_i$ is normal in $G_{i+1}$ and every factor $G_{i+1}/G_i$ is abelian (equivalently, $G$ is solvable).

Suppose $G$ is a group with the property that every countable subgroup of $G$ has a subnormal abelian series. Must $G$ itself have a subnormal abelian series?
